caption: This drawing is an illustrated map labeled "The M. Ward Estate – The Blackwell Survey 1860," featuring a landscaped garden and estate grounds. The drawing uses colors such as green for grass, trees, and shrubbery; beige and tan for pathways and roads; red and pink for flowerbeds and garden designs; blue for some garden sections; gray and brown for rocks and structures; and yellow as background. The central area showcases symmetrical formal gardens composed of rectangular and circular plots, each filled with intricate geometric arrangements of flowers and hedges, bordered by straight and curved paths. Two large circular garden areas with star patterns are positioned in the lower left and middle left portions, with rectangular garden beds adjacent. A semicircular enclosed area is present in the middle, containing internal garden beds and a round central feature. In the upper left corner, a translucent structure houses a nude statue, rendered in faint gray, with radiating lines suggesting glass or crystal casing. The top right shows a rocky hill with a yellow-brown structure atop, surrounded by trees. Trees and shrubs, depicted in varying shades of green, are scattered throughout the estate, with denser groupings along the edges and near structures. The lower right corner includes an inset circle displaying a close-up of a five-pointed star-shaped garden bed filled with alternating red and purple sections. The overall composition is organized in a bird’s-eye view, showing the systematic arrangement of gardens, paths, and natural features of the estate.
title: M. Ward Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
